caption.en: 🗻 ACT Math Advanced — Score Range 28–36 Topics

rows.en: Sequences, integer properties, modular arithmetic, complex numbers
Polynomial systems, rational equations, logarithms, exponentials
Piecewise, recursive, parametric, function composition chains
Radians, unit circle, identities, inverse trig, law of sines/cosines
Limits (informal), sequences/series, conic sections, polar basics
Circle theorems, similarity, 3D solids, geometric proof
Permutations, combinations, expected value, normal dist., regression

body.en: ACT Math 2 is an advanced subject-level mathematics course for students who have completed standard ACT Math preparation and wish to extend their skills into pre-calculus territory — the topics that appear in the hardest ACT questions and on ACT subject tests.

This course covers the top-difficulty ACT Math topics: advanced algebra, pre-calculus functions, matrices, advanced trigonometry, and non-routine geometry. It is also ideal preparation for the ACT Subject Test in Mathematics, which tests material through pre-calculus.

label.en: ⏱ ACT Subject Math 1 Pacing & Time Management Strategy

body.en:
• Pacing Baseline: 50 questions in 60 minutes = 72 seconds per question. There is no guessing penalty — every unanswered question is a lost opportunity.
  • Three-Pass Strategy: Pass 1 (Questions 1–25, ~20 min): bank easy points rapidly. Pass 2 (Questions 26–45, ~25 min): methodical solving of mid-level algebra, trig, and coordinate geometry. Pass 3 (Questions 46–50 & review, ~15 min): tackle non-routine multi-step items and ensure all bubble answers are filled.
  • Approved Calculator Fluency: Graphing calculators are permitted throughout. Store formulas, use matrix inverse/determinant functions, and verify complex number arithmetic \(a + bi\) directly.

label.en: ▲ The 4 Core Commandments for Scoring 30+ on ACT Advanced Math

body.en:
• 1. Never Leave Blanks: Unlike old SAT Subject tests, there is zero penalty for incorrect answers. If time is running short with 2 minutes remaining, pick a favorite letter (e.g., C or D) and fill every remaining bubble.
  • 2. Identify Conic Signatures at a Glance: In \(Ax^2 + Bxy + Cy^2 + Dx + Ey + F = 0\), same signs on \(x^2\) and \(y^2\) with \(A = C\) indicates a circle; same signs with \(A \neq C\) indicates an ellipse; opposite signs indicates a hyperbola; only one squared term indicates a parabola.
  • 3. Exploit Backsolving & Number Substitution: When an algebraic equation has complex fractions, logs, or radicals, testing answer choice C (the median value) first often eliminates 2–3 options in under 30 seconds.
  • 4. Memorize the Critical Edge-Case Formulas: Circle inscribed angle \(=\frac{1}{2}\text{central}\), Heron's formula \(A = \sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}\), sum of infinite geometric series \(S_\infty = \frac{a}{1-r}\), and vector dot product \(\vec{u}\cdot\vec{v} = u_1 v_1 + u_2 v_2\).
